reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 09, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA, full white/cyan/alpha review sheet and unchanged naiwa.png; checked three-quarter pose, cap, covered hair and brow shadow, narrow upper-lip area versus beard, one mouth, uniform/collar/ribbon/pendant, crop, lighting, collar fit, complete card/note/backplate and visible transparency.

entries.positive_observation: The dark olive peaked cap with small gold front detail and gold visor leaves, covered hair and dark under-visor brow area remain. The narrow upper-lip region has not broadened into a moustache mass or beard; the chin is smooth and there is one serious closed mouth, with no spectacles. The three-quarter head turn and gaze toward viewer left are preserved rather than rotated frontal, with chest-up crop, warm directional light and strong visor shadow. The dark olive uniform keeps two pale patterned collar patches, gold shoulder trim at viewer left, one pale blue-white neck ribbon and one small silver-toned neck pendant. The high collar fits coherently around a short broad neck beneath the rounded chin, without a stalk, pinching, clipping or cream bib. The complete tilted dark frame, opaque muted gray-olive photographic backplate, overlapping warm-cream note with compact upper marks and mostly blank lower paper, and small dark right-edge tab remain. Full white/cyan inspection shows a genuine transparent exterior without visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte halo.
entries.alpha_decision: Accept native RGBA extrema 0..254 after actual white/cyan/alpha viewing; no source-alpha replacement was performed or needed, and near-opacity values alone were not rejection grounds.
entries.visible_limitations: At 65x67 the narrow upper-lip pixels do not reliably distinguish fine hair from shadow, and exact cap, collar and neck insignia cannot be read; the review confirms no clear broad facial-hair addition and compares only visible forms and placements. Note marks remain indistinct rather than readable text.
